messages.content: 一位化學家正在進行一個實驗，使用一個2公斤的特定物質A樣本。實驗開始時，該物質的初始溫度為攝氏25度。然後，化學家將物質加熱到最終溫度攝氏75度。該實驗在1大氣壓力下進行。化學家重複進行相同物質的實驗，但這次的初始溫度為攝氏10度，最終溫度為攝氏50度。你能計算出在這兩個實驗的設定初始和最終條件下，物質的熵變化嗎？

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Entropy change for a reversible heating process**

For a material heated reversibly from an initial temperature \(T_{\text{i}}\) to a final temperature \(T_{\text{f}}\) at constant pressure, the change in entropy is  

\[
\Delta S \;=\;\int_{T_{\text{i}}}^{T_{\text{f}}}\frac{\delta Q_{\text{rev}}}{T}
          \;=\;\int_{T_{\text{i}}}^{T_{\text{f}}}\frac{m\,c_{p}\,dT}{T}
          \;=\;m\,c_{p}\,\ln\!\left(\frac{T_{\text{f}}}{T_{\text{i}}}\right)
\]

where  
* \(m\) – mass of the sample (kg),  
* \(c_{p}\) – specific heat capacity at constant pressure (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹),  
* temperatures are expressed in Kelvin.

---

### 1. First experiment  
* Mass \(m = 2\;\text{kg}\)  
* Initial temperature \(T_{\text{i}} = 25^{\circ}\text{C} = 298.15\;\text{K}\)  
* Final temperature \(T_{\text{f}} = 75^{\circ}\text{C} = 348.15\;\text{K}\)

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle 
\Delta S_{1}=2\,c_{p}\,
            \ln\!\left(\frac{348.15}{298.15}\right)}
\]

If you know the value of \(c_{p}\) for substance A, just plug it in.  
*(Example: for water, \(c_{p}\approx 4180\;\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\), giving \(\Delta S_{1}\approx 1.30\times10^{3}\;\text{J K}^{-1}\).)*

---

### 2. Second experiment  
* Mass \(m = 2\;\text{kg}\)  
* Initial temperature \(T_{\text{i}} = 10^{\circ}\text{C} = 283.15\;\text{K}\)  
* Final temperature \(T_{\text{f}} = 50^{\circ}\text{C} = 323.15\;\text{K}\)

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle 
\Delta S_{2}=2\,c_{p}\,
            \ln\!\left(\frac{323.15}{283.15}\right)}
\]

*(Using the same water example gives \(\Delta S_{2}\approx 1.11\times10^{3}\;\text{J K}^{-1}\).)*

---

#### What you need next
To obtain numerical results, simply insert the specific heat capacity \(c_{p}\) of your particular substance A into the formulas above. If you can tell me what \(c_{p}\) is (or the identity of substance A so I can look up its typical \(c_{p}\)), I’ll give you the exact entropy changes in joules per kelvin.
